articles.text: MǓQIN: Xiǎo Lín, chīle fàn bú yào niàn shū le, xiūxi xiūxi ba!
MOTHER: Xiǎo Lín, don't study any more after dinner, just relax a bit!
XIǍO LÍN: Hǎo. Nín yào hē chá ma? Wǒ qù dào.
XIǍO LÍN: Okay. Do you want to drink some tea? I'll go pour it.
MǓQIN: Děng yíxià, ràng wo kànkan, nǐde máoyī shi bu shi pò le? Míngtian wǒ děi qù gěi ni mǎi jiàn xīnde.
MOTHER: Wait a second, let me see — is your sweater torn? Tomorrow I'll have to go buy you a new one.
XIǍO LÍN: Mā, wǒ bú yào xīnde, zhèijiàn hái kěyi chuān ne.
XIǍO LÍN: Mom, I don't want a new one. I can still wear this one.
MǓQIN: Tiān lěng le, nǐ xūyào yíjiàn xīn máoyī, wǒ huì gěi ni yùbèihǎo. Míngnián nǐ shàng dàxuéde shíhou, wǒ huì duō gěi ni yùbèi jǐjiàn xīn yīfu.
MOTHER: The weather's getting cold, you need a new sweater. I'll get one ready for you. Next year when you go to college I'll get a few more new things ready for you to wear.
XIǍO LÍN: Bú yòng le, wǒ bù xiǎng shàng dàxué le.
XIǍO LÍN: You don't need to, I don't want to go to college anymore.
MǓQIN: Wèishénme? Nǐ bú shi yào xué yī ma?
MOTHER: Why not? Don't you want to study medicine?
XIǍO LÍN: Bù shǎo rén shuō bú shàng dàxué yě kěyi gōngzuò, yě yíyàng kěyi shēnghuó. Wèishénme yídìng yào shàng dàxué ne?
XIǍO LÍN: A lot of people say that you can work and live just the same without going to college. Why is it necessary to go to college?
MǓQIN: Zhèizhǒng huà xiànzài hěn liúxíng, kěshi wǒ xiǎng zhè huà bú tài duì.
MOTHER: This kind of talk is very popular these days, but I don't think it's very true.
XIǍO LÍN: Wèishénme? Yǒude rén zài dàxuéli pīnmìng niàn shū, xiàng wǒmen jiā duìmiànde Zhōu Xiānsheng, duì shùxué nàme yǒu yánjiū, déle shuòshì, bóshì, hái bú shi zhǎobudào gōngzuò!

XIǍO LÍN: Why not? Some people study like mad at a university, like Mr. Zhōu who lives across from us; he's such an expert in mathematics, he's got a Master's degree and a Ph.D., and isn't he still unable to find a job!
MǓQIN: Zhōu Xiānshengde qíngxing gēn biérén bù tóng. Suīrán tā xiāngdāng yǒu zhīshi, kěshi tā bù xǐhuande gōngzuò tā jiù bú zuò, nà dāngrán bù róngyi zhǎodào gōngzuò.
MOTHER: Mr. Zhōu's situation is different from other people's. Although he is quite knowledgeable, he won't take a job he doesn't like. So of course it isn't easy for him to find a job.
XIǍO LÍN: Duì le, tā bù xǐhuan zuò lǎoshī, tā jiù xǐhuan xiě wénzhāng. Zài Zhōngxuéshēng zhōukānshang wǒ hái kànjianguo tāde wénzhāng ne!
XIǍO LÍN: Right. He doesn't like to be a teacher, he just likes to write articles. I've even seen his articles in the weekly High School Student!
MǓQIN: Tāde wénzhāng hǎo bu hǎo?
MOTHER: Are his articles good?
XIǍO LÍN: Hǎo, kěshi bù róngyi dǒng, zhōngxuéshēng kàn zhèiyàngde wénzhāng tài nán le.
XIǍO LÍN: Yes, but they're not easy to understand. They're too hard for high school students to read.

MǓQIN: Suǒyǐ, nǐ bù néng shuō Zhōu Xiānshengde qíngxing jiù shi dàjiāde qíngxing. Wǒ xiǎng, kěyi zhèiyàng shuō: niànguo hěn duō shūde rén bù yídìng yǒu hěn hǎode gōngzuò. Kěshi duō niàn yìdiǎnr shū duì zhǎo gōngzuò yídìng yǒu bāngzhu.

MOTHER: So you can't say that Mr. Zhōu's situation is everyone's situation. I think you might say this: someone who has had a lot of education doesn't necessarily get a very good job. But getting more education will certainly be helpful in looking for a job.
XIǍO LÍN: Kěshi, wǒde jǐge tóngxué gāozhōng méiyou niànwán jiù zuò shì le, xiànzài tāmende shēnghuó dōu bú yòng kào fùmǔ le, tāmen dōu dúlì le.
XIǍO LÍN: But several classmates of mine started working before they had finished high school, and now they don't have to depend on their parents to support them; they're all independent.
MǓQIN: Dànshi wǒ xiǎng, shèhuì háishi xūyào yǒu zhīshide rén, shèhuì yuè fādá yuè xūyào yǒu zhīshi. Nǐ shuō duì bu duì?
MOTHER: But I think that society still needs knowledgeable people. The more developed society is, the more it needs knowledge. Don't you think so?
XIǍO LÍN: Duì!
XIǍO LÍN: Right!
MǓQIN: Nàme hǎo le, nǐ niàn dàxuéde shì zěnmeyàng?
MOTHER: All right then, what about the matter of your going to college?
XIǍO LÍN: Mm... wǒ zài xiǎngyixiǎng.
XIǍO LÍN: Mm... I'll think it over some more.
MǓQIN: Hǎo, wǒmen míngtian zài tántan.
MOTHER: Okay, we'll talk more about it tomorrow.
